world.title: U.S. watchdog investigates ambassador to Greece over alleged $100,000 payment request
world.summary: The State Department inspector general is investigating U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and the embassy she leads after Trump donor Eric Deters accused her of seeking $100,000 to pay her credit card debt in exchange for access to senior administration officials, according to people familiar with the inquir
world.content: The State Department inspector general is investigating U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and the embassy she leads after Trump donor Eric Deters accused her of seeking $100,000 to pay her credit card debt in exchange for access to senior administration officials, according to people familiar with the inquiry. Deters, a lawyer and political consultant, said he did not pay; Guilfoyle’s lawyer disputed the authenticity of the messages he provided. Deters said the request came shortly before Guilfoyle’s 2025 confirmation hearing. The messages he supplied reportedly include a request to transfer funds directly to American Express so the payment “won’t show up anywhere”. Vice President JD Vance said the allegations should be assessed on the facts, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he did not know whether the account was true. The inspector general’s office does not confirm or deny investigations, and the State Department declined to comment.
world.image_alt: U.S. watchdog investigates ambassador to Greece over alleged $100,000 payment request

world.title: French student protests spread as arrests top 6,600 and police tactics face scrutiny
world.summary: French high-school protests have spread nationwide, with hundreds of thousands demonstrating on Oct. 6 and more than 6,600 young people arrested during the crackdown, according to figures cited by German daily taz. Hundreds of students, teachers and police officers have been injured, Taiwan’s Storm Media reported; one
world.content: French high-school protests have spread nationwide, with hundreds of thousands demonstrating on Oct. 6 and more than 6,600 young people arrested during the crackdown, according to figures cited by German daily taz. Hundreds of students, teachers and police officers have been injured, Taiwan’s Storm Media reported; one 15-year-old lost a hand when a grenade exploded. The scale of the arrests has drawn scrutiny because most detainees were minors. Students cite teacher shortages, school buildings in poor condition, crowded classes and pressure over university admissions. The French government said police would stop using flashbang grenades against young demonstrators. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu offered students three hours of talks and said he would present proposals in a month; student organizations rejected the offer as an “alibi”. Further mass protests are planned for Oct. 17, Daily News Egypt reported.
world.image_alt: French student protests spread as arrests top 6,600 and police tactics face scrutiny

world.title: Category 4 Hurricane Simon threatens Mexico with flooding and mudslides
world.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 off Mexico’s Pacific coast on Saturday. The National Hurricane Center reported maximum sustained winds of 150 mph and forecast that the storm would reach or move just inland of the west-central coast on Sunday. Forecasters warned of 10 to 20 inches of rain across southwestern
world.content: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 off Mexico’s Pacific coast on Saturday. The National Hurricane Center reported maximum sustained winds of 150 mph and forecast that the storm would reach or move just inland of the west-central coast on Sunday. Forecasters warned of 10 to 20 inches of rain across southwestern Mexico, with as much as 30 inches in isolated areas, along with life-threatening flooding, mudslides, destructive coastal waves and storm surge. Authorities in Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities, began evacuating at-risk residents and urged hotels in Puerto Vallarta to move workers and visitors to shelters or safe locations. Mexico’s Navy had evacuated about 100 people from coastal settlements, while Jalisco declared a red alert and Puerto Vallarta’s airport suspended operations. Simon’s slow northward movement and rain bands had already caused flooding in Acapulco, and forecasters warned that conditions could worsen as the storm approached land.
world.image_alt: Category 4 Hurricane Simon threatens Mexico with flooding and mudslides

world.title: Pope condemns death penalty as Pentagon plans livestreamed Fort Hood execution
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV called the death penalty “inadmissible” on Oct. 10, saying it violates human dignity, as the U.S. military plans to livestream the Dec. 3 firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan at Fort Hood, Texas. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 in a 2009 shooting
world.content: Pope Leo XIV called the death penalty “inadmissible” on Oct. 10, saying it violates human dignity, as the U.S. military plans to livestream the Dec. 3 firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan at Fort Hood, Texas. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 in a 2009 shooting at the base. Leo’s social media post marked the World Day Against the Death Penalty and did not directly mention Hasan or the U.S. plan. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s announcement drew condemnation from Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin and U.S. bishops’ conference president Archbishop Paul Coakley. President Donald Trump said Hasan would be executed by firing squad but indicated he would make the final decision on broadcasting the execution. Vice President JD Vance said he did not know whether the livestream would happen.
world.image_alt: Pope condemns death penalty as Pentagon plans livestreamed Fort Hood execution

world.title: WHO reports no plague cases as Russian lab death remains unexplained
world.summary: The World Health Organization said it still cannot determine the cause of the pneumonia that killed a 28-year-old worker at a plague research institute in Russia’s Irkutsk region on Oct. 2. It said it has found no evidence of ongoing transmission or any registered plague case. Russia told the WHO that tests for high-th
world.content: The World Health Organization said it still cannot determine the cause of the pneumonia that killed a 28-year-old worker at a plague research institute in Russia’s Irkutsk region on Oct. 2. It said it has found no evidence of ongoing transmission or any registered plague case. Russia told the WHO that tests for high-threat pathogens on the worker and her contacts were negative; her contacts had no symptoms, and authorities identified no further linked cases of severe pneumonia. Russian officials said they conducted more than 5,500 tests, but the cause of death remains unconfirmed, leaving the WHO unable to assess the event with confidence. About 200 people were initially quarantined, and a local official said 60% had been released by Oct. 6. The WHO said it will continue to monitor the situation and reassess its public-health implications as more information becomes available.
world.image_alt: WHO reports no plague cases as Russian lab death remains unexplained

world.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections until September 2027, citing Israeli restrictions
world.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections scheduled for Nov. 28 and scheduled both legislative and presidential votes for Sept. 11, 2027, moving the presidential poll from early next year. The legislative election would be the first since 2006, and Abbas won the last presidential vote in 2005.
world.content: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections scheduled for Nov. 28 and scheduled both legislative and presidential votes for Sept. 11, 2027, moving the presidential poll from early next year. The legislative election would be the first since 2006, and Abbas won the last presidential vote in 2005. Abbas’s decree blamed Israeli measures and said conditions for free, fair and inclusive voting were not in place. In the West Bank and East Jerusalem, it cited military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence, movement restrictions and Israel’s withholding of Palestinian tax revenue. In Gaza, it cited exceptional security and humanitarian conditions, the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces and stalled reconstruction. The decree also said restrictions on access for election officials and international observers complicated preparations in Gaza and East Jerusalem. The Palestinian Authority has faced international pressure, including from the European Union, to hold elections as part of reforms. Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009, and the Palestinian Legislative Council has not met since 2007.
world.image_alt: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections until September 2027, citing Israeli restrictions

world.title: Pro-Palestinian rallies span cities worldwide as Gaza war enters fourth year
world.summary: Pro-Palestinian demonstrations took place in London, Berlin, Dublin, Rome, Brussels and Australian cities on Oct. 10 and 11, as protesters marked three years since the Gaza war began and demanded an end to Israeli attacks. In London, the Palestine Solidarity Campaign said more than 250,000 people joined the rally, a fi
world.content: Pro-Palestinian demonstrations took place in London, Berlin, Dublin, Rome, Brussels and Australian cities on Oct. 10 and 11, as protesters marked three years since the Gaza war began and demanded an end to Israeli attacks. In London, the Palestine Solidarity Campaign said more than 250,000 people joined the rally, a figure JTA said was not independently verified. Berlin police estimated about 3,500 marchers, while Irish broadcaster RTÉ reported more than 10,000 at a Dublin march. Demonstrators called on governments to halt arms sales to Israel and impose sanctions. The rallies coincided with the anniversary of Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack, which killed 1,221 people in Israel and took 251 hostage, according to an AFP tally. Gaza’s Health Ministry says Israel’s subsequent offensive has killed more than 74,200 Palestinians, including at least 1,450 since a ceasefire took effect in October 2025. Israeli strikes have continued despite the ceasefire. Israel rejects allegations that it is committing genocide, and the International Court of Justice has not made such a finding. London police said they arrested 20 people, including two carrying signs supporting Palestine Action, which is banned in Britain. Officers also imposed route and face-covering restrictions. In Germany, protesters criticized arms exports to Israel. The government authorized military equipment exports worth about €736 million in the second quarter of 2026, according to the German parliament.
world.image_alt: Pro-Palestinian rallies span cities worldwide as Gaza war enters fourth year

world.title: Landslide-triggered Nepal flood sweeps away homes and bridges, prompts evacuations
world.summary: A flash flood on Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River swept away homes and bridges in Gorkha district on Sunday, Oct. 11, after a landslide reportedly blocked the river and sent muddy water downstream. Authorities ordered riverside communities to evacuate. Four people were reported missing, while officials said there were no co
world.content: A flash flood on Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River swept away homes and bridges in Gorkha district on Sunday, Oct. 11, after a landslide reportedly blocked the river and sent muddy water downstream. Authorities ordered riverside communities to evacuate. Four people were reported missing, while officials said there were no confirmed casualties in initial updates. Damage estimates rose as officials assessed the area. Gorkha’s chief district officer initially cited about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges, while local reports said at least 35 homes and six bridges were swept away. The flood also damaged a hydroelectric project camp and washed away a highway bridge linking Gorkha with Dhading. Authorities told residents in Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi to move to safer ground. The army rescued six people near Jagat, and 18 workers escaped from the damaged project camp. Police and army personnel reached the area and monitored conditions from a helicopter.
world.image_alt: Landslide-triggered Nepal flood sweeps away homes and bridges, prompts evacuations

business.title: Gulf oil and gas output remains curtailed as Isaias weakens
business.summary: Gulf producers kept 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production shut in on Saturday after Hurricane Isaias weakened to a post-tropical system; 113 offshore platforms, about 30% of the Gulf total, remained evacuated. Shell and Chevron began sending personnel back to offshore assets as conditions improved, while
business.content: Gulf producers kept 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production shut in on Saturday after Hurricane Isaias weakened to a post-tropical system; 113 offshore platforms, about 30% of the Gulf total, remained evacuated. Shell and Chevron began sending personnel back to offshore assets as conditions improved, while the U.S. Energy Department authorized an exchange of up to 4 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address supply disruptions. Isaias could cause insured losses in the single-digit billions of dollars, according to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Matthew Palazola. He said stronger Florida building codes could limit damage, while recent insurance-market reforms had not yet faced a major test.
business.image_alt: Gulf oil and gas output remains curtailed as Isaias weakens

business.title: Musk sees a path for SpaceX to be worth far more than Earth’s economy
business.summary: Elon Musk said he sees a path for SpaceX to become worth “orders of magnitude” more than Earth’s current economy. Business Insider estimated that could imply a valuation above $12 quadrillion—about 5,500 times the company’s reported $2.2 trillion market capitalization. The comparison uses projected annual global output
business.content: Elon Musk said he sees a path for SpaceX to become worth “orders of magnitude” more than Earth’s current economy. Business Insider estimated that could imply a valuation above $12 quadrillion—about 5,500 times the company’s reported $2.2 trillion market capitalization. The comparison uses projected annual global output of $126 trillion as a reference, although annual economic output and a company’s market valuation measure different things. On Oct. 9, Musk clarified that he was not expressing strong confidence in that outcome, only that the probability of reaching it was “not zero”. SpaceX reported second-quarter revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% year over year, and a net loss of $541 million. Analysts cited the costs and risks of operating beyond Earth as barriers to reaching the scale implied by the projection.
business.image_alt: Musk sees a path for SpaceX to be worth far more than Earth’s economy

business.title: Analysts say Russian diesel deal will barely ease US fuel prices
business.summary: Energy analysts say Russian diesel shipments are unlikely to provide sustained relief from high U.S. fuel prices. Bloomberg economist Chris Kennedy estimated that the planned November volume would equal roughly one day of U.S. consumption. Damage to Russian refineries, delivery logistics and possible legal restrictions
business.content: Energy analysts say Russian diesel shipments are unlikely to provide sustained relief from high U.S. fuel prices. Bloomberg economist Chris Kennedy estimated that the planned November volume would equal roughly one day of U.S. consumption. Damage to Russian refineries, delivery logistics and possible legal restrictions leave it unclear how much diesel can reach buyers. Reuters reported that Russian diesel and gasoil exports fell to about 144,000 barrels a day in September, from as much as 270,000 in August. The International Energy Agency estimates that Russian diesel production capacity has fallen by nearly a third after Ukrainian strikes. Analysts say redirecting fuel to the United States could leave Russia’s existing customers seeking replacement supplies rather than adding equivalent volumes to the global market. Separately, three industry sources told Reuters that President Donald Trump was expected in the coming days to direct federal departments to find ways to curb diesel prices. Options could include using the Defense Production Act and bypassing state and local rules that restrict energy production.
business.image_alt: Analysts say Russian diesel deal will barely ease US fuel prices

business.title: India opens dollar window for oil firms and tightens rupee trading
business.summary: The Reserve Bank of India will supply dollars directly to three state-owned oil companies starting Monday, Oct. 12, and tighten currency-derivative rules to curb pressure on the rupee, which is near a record low. The RBI’s special window covers the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petrol
business.content: The Reserve Bank of India will supply dollars directly to three state-owned oil companies starting Monday, Oct. 12, and tighten currency-derivative rules to curb pressure on the rupee, which is near a record low. The RBI’s special window covers the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum, diverting their purchases from the open foreign-exchange market. The currency has weakened more than 7% this year as oil prices and overseas yields rose. The new rules also make certain rupee hedges costlier and reduce the size of positions firms can take without proof of an underlying business exposure. The dollar facility draws on the central bank’s reserves, which fell by more than $50 billion in recent weeks to about $734 billion as of Oct. 2. The RBI said the oil companies could begin using the facility on Monday; it will remain open until further notice.
business.image_alt: India opens dollar window for oil firms and tightens rupee trading

business.title: Justice Department probes five TV networks over Trump press-pool boycott
business.summary: The Justice Department is investigating whether ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC violated federal antitrust law when they briefly stopped providing White House press-pool coverage after President Trump barred three news organizations from the grounds. The department sent the networks civil investigative demands on Frida
business.content: The Justice Department is investigating whether ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC violated federal antitrust law when they briefly stopped providing White House press-pool coverage after President Trump barred three news organizations from the grounds. The department sent the networks civil investigative demands on Friday, saying group boycotts by commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act. The press pool divides filming duties among networks and distributes video and audio to other outlets. The networks suspended pool coverage after the White House revoked credentials for CNN, MS Now and Politico. The three organizations sued, and a judge ordered their access temporarily restored. A federal judge extended that order this week to Tuesday while considering the case, though the White House has continued to bar CNN and Politico from the Oval Office and Air Force One.
business.image_alt: Justice Department probes five TV networks over Trump press-pool boycott

business.title: Nvidia weighs buying or expanding its stake in open-model startup Reflection AI
business.summary: Nvidia is in early-stage talks to acquire U.S. AI startup Reflection AI or increase its investment. Options include a full purchase, hiring key staff and licensing technology, or providing more capital and computing resources. The talks could lead to an agreement in the coming weeks but may also fall through, and terms
business.content: Nvidia is in early-stage talks to acquire U.S. AI startup Reflection AI or increase its investment. Options include a full purchase, hiring key staff and licensing technology, or providing more capital and computing resources. The talks could lead to an agreement in the coming weeks but may also fall through, and terms remain undetermined. Reflection develops open-weight AI models that customers can adapt and run on their own hardware, potentially at lower operating costs than leading closed models. Nvidia is working to expand the open-model ecosystem, and the Trump administration has said it hopes Reflection can compete with lower-cost Chinese alternatives such as DeepSeek. Reflection recently introduced Beam, a model aimed at coding and AI-agent tasks.
business.image_alt: Nvidia weighs buying or expanding its stake in open-model startup Reflection AI

business.title: Investors warn AI borrowing and data-center spending raise market risks
business.summary: Investors and strategists warn that heavy reliance on AI-related shares, rising borrowing and large data-center spending plans could leave markets vulnerable if earnings fall short of expectations. They question whether AI revenue can justify the scale and pace of investment as portfolios become increasingly dependent
business.content: Investors and strategists warn that heavy reliance on AI-related shares, rising borrowing and large data-center spending plans could leave markets vulnerable if earnings fall short of expectations. They question whether AI revenue can justify the scale and pace of investment as portfolios become increasingly dependent on the technology build-out. Joachim Klement of Panmure Liberum predicts the AI boom could end in 2027 or 2028, arguing that a slowdown in expansion plans could weaken earnings across the supply chain. Ray Dalio has also warned that higher rates and investor profit-taking could trigger a downturn, while Galaxy Digital founder Michael Novogratz argues that AI stock valuations remain attractive and the rally can continue.
business.image_alt: Investors warn AI borrowing and data-center spending raise market risks

business.title: AI-related borrowing falls below half of August total as investors reassess risk
business.summary: Technology companies raised $23 billion in AI-related debt in September, less than half the previous month’s total, as investors reassessed the risks of financing data centers and other AI infrastructure. Issuance peaked at a record $113 billion in June, and AI-related bond issuance in the U.S. investment-grade market
business.content: Technology companies raised $23 billion in AI-related debt in September, less than half the previous month’s total, as investors reassessed the risks of financing data centers and other AI infrastructure. Issuance peaked at a record $113 billion in June, and AI-related bond issuance in the U.S. investment-grade market halted in September. Banks are assembling a $60 billion financing package for Broadcom and Anthropic, while SpaceX is negotiating to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips. About $18 billion in loans tied to Oracle’s Project Jupiter data center campus came under pressure after the site had difficulty securing electricity.
business.image_alt: AI-related borrowing falls below half of August total as investors reassess risk

science.title: IceCube physicist Francis Halzen wins Nobel for neutrino observatory
science.summary: Francis Halzen, a founding leader of the IceCube Collaboration, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for work associated with the Antarctic neutrino observatory, NASA said in its Oct. 11 astronomy feature. A Reuters headline listed by Mirage News identifies Halzen as the Nobel physics prize winner. IceCube uses nearly 1
science.content: Francis Halzen, a founding leader of the IceCube Collaboration, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for work associated with the Antarctic neutrino observatory, NASA said in its Oct. 11 astronomy feature. A Reuters headline listed by Mirage News identifies Halzen as the Nobel physics prize winner. IceCube uses nearly 100 detector strings embedded in ice near the South Pole to search for high-energy neutrinos from powerful cosmic processes. Each string carries basketball-sized light sensors lowered into a melted shaft. Once the water refreezes, the instruments detect blue light produced when particles from neutrino collisions move through the surrounding ice. NASA described IceCube as the largest neutrino detector ever built.
science.image_alt: IceCube physicist Francis Halzen wins Nobel for neutrino observatory

science.title: Study finds Himalayan flood-zone construction rose 45% in seven years
science.summary: A study estimates that nearly 300,000 people in Himalayan regions of Nepal, India and China live in areas potentially exposed to flooding. It also found that buildings covered about 45% more area in potential flood zones in 2023 than in 2016. The study, published in Scientific Reports, examined hazards including floods
science.content: A study estimates that nearly 300,000 people in Himalayan regions of Nepal, India and China live in areas potentially exposed to flooding. It also found that buildings covered about 45% more area in potential flood zones in 2023 than in 2016. The study, published in Scientific Reports, examined hazards including floods linked to glacial lakes. Researchers examined 1,361 Himalayan lakes, according to a study summary.
science.image_alt: Study finds Himalayan flood-zone construction rose 45% in seven years

science.title: Strong solar storm brings northern lights to southern UK skies
science.summary: The northern lights were visible across the United Kingdom on Saturday, Oct. 10, with sightings as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent after geomagnetic activity reached 600 nanoteslas. The Met Office said clear skies could allow further sightings in Scotland and at similar geomagnetic longitudes through Tuesday, Oc
science.content: The northern lights were visible across the United Kingdom on Saturday, Oct. 10, with sightings as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent after geomagnetic activity reached 600 nanoteslas. The Met Office said clear skies could allow further sightings in Scotland and at similar geomagnetic longitudes through Tuesday, Oct. 13. The display followed two glancing coronal mass ejections and a high-speed stream from a coronal hole. These can intensify auroral activity as charged solar particles interact with Earth’s magnetic field and upper atmosphere. Photographers also captured the aurora in south Wales, including around Caldicot, Loughor and Pembrokeshire.
science.image_alt: Strong solar storm brings northern lights to southern UK skies

science.title: Gene therapy and goggles restore limited vision to blind patients
science.summary: An experimental gene therapy paired with camera-equipped goggles improved light sensitivity in seven of nine people with advanced retinitis pigmentosa who completed follow-up; six had clinically meaningful gains, researchers reported in a study published Oct. 7 in the New England Journal of Medicine. Some participants
science.content: An experimental gene therapy paired with camera-equipped goggles improved light sensitivity in seven of nine people with advanced retinitis pigmentosa who completed follow-up; six had clinically meaningful gains, researchers reported in a study published Oct. 7 in the New England Journal of Medicine. Some participants could locate a doorway or follow a line, but they still could not read or recognize faces. The phase 1 trial enrolled 10 people and primarily assessed safety. Researchers injected the eye with poorer vision with genetic instructions for ChrimsonR, which makes surviving retinal cells responsive to light. The goggles convert camera images into pulses of amber light. Follow-up studies are planned, but the research institute said it could not yet provide details of a phase 2 trial.
science.image_alt: Gene therapy and goggles restore limited vision to blind patients

science.title: Category 4 Hurricane Simon threatens Mexico
science.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 on Saturday as it approached Mexico’s west-central Pacific coast, with maximum sustained winds of up to 155 mph. The U.S. National Hurricane Center forecast 10 to 20 inches of rain across parts of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals reaching 30 inches, and
science.content: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 on Saturday as it approached Mexico’s west-central Pacific coast, with maximum sustained winds of up to 155 mph. The U.S. National Hurricane Center forecast 10 to 20 inches of rain across parts of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals reaching 30 inches, and warned of life-threatening flooding and mudslides. The storm was expected to reach the coast or move just inland on Sunday, Oct. 11, bringing a risk of destructive waves and storm surge near landfall. Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating people from at-risk areas; officials also urged Puerto Vallarta hotels and tourism businesses to ensure workers and visitors could reach shelters.

science.title: Autism genetics differ more by diagnosis timing than by sex
science.summary: A study in *Behavior Genetics* found that autism’s common genetic profile was highly similar in males and females but differed more between people diagnosed early and late. The genetic correlation was 0.81 between male and female autism, compared with 0.42 between early- and late-diagnosed autism. Across 68 traits, lat
science.content: A study in *Behavior Genetics* found that autism’s common genetic profile was highly similar in males and females but differed more between people diagnosed early and late. The genetic correlation was 0.81 between male and female autism, compared with 0.42 between early- and late-diagnosed autism. Across 68 traits, late-diagnosed autism showed stronger genetic links with depression, PTSD, ADHD and social difficulties, while early-diagnosed autism had stronger links with educational attainment and some cognitive measures. A separate study in the *American Journal of Human Genetics* identified small changes in the X-chromosome gene MECP2 as candidates that may help explain why boys receive autism diagnoses about four times as often as girls.
science.image_alt: Autism genetics differ more by diagnosis timing than by sex

science.title: Brazil prosecutors seek $108 million from Shell over 2024 floods
science.summary: Brazilian prosecutors filed a civil lawsuit seeking 540 million reais, about $108 million, from Shell’s Brazilian subsidiary for damages linked to the deadly 2024 floods in Rio Grande do Sul. Prosecutors argue that Shell should bear a share of the losses proportional to its parent company’s historical contribution to g
science.content: Brazilian prosecutors filed a civil lawsuit seeking 540 million reais, about $108 million, from Shell’s Brazilian subsidiary for damages linked to the deadly 2024 floods in Rio Grande do Sul. Prosecutors argue that Shell should bear a share of the losses proportional to its parent company’s historical contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions, which they estimate at 2%. Torrential rains and flooding in April and May 2024 killed nearly 200 people and displaced about half a million, according to reports on the lawsuit. Prosecutors and environmental group Instituto Preservar filed the claim, seeking compensation for collective environmental and moral harm as well as material damage. Shell told AFP it had not received formal notice of the case.
science.image_alt: Brazil prosecutors seek $108 million from Shell over 2024 floods

science.title: French ESA astronaut returns after record 237-day space station mission
science.summary: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Europe on Oct. 10, landing in Cologne after spending 237 days, five hours and 18 minutes aboard the International Space Station with Crew-12. Her mission set a European record for a single spaceflight, surpassing Luca Parmitano’s previous mark by more than 35 days. Adenot launche
science.content: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Europe on Oct. 10, landing in Cologne after spending 237 days, five hours and 18 minutes aboard the International Space Station with Crew-12. Her mission set a European record for a single spaceflight, surpassing Luca Parmitano’s previous mark by more than 35 days. Adenot launched on Feb. 13; Crew-12 undocked on Oct. 7 and splashed down on Oct. 8 before travelling to Houston for initial post-flight activities. She will spend two to three weeks adjusting to Earth’s gravity and participating in data collection at the German Aerospace Center’s:envihab facility near the European Astronaut Centre, then continue rehabilitation and follow-up.
science.image_alt: French ESA astronaut returns after record 237-day space station mission

sports.title: Matt Renshaw’s 190 lifts Australia after collapse in Durban Test
sports.summary: Matt Renshaw scored a career-best 190 to lift Australia to 390 all out in the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead after the visitors slumped to 124 for six. His 134-run ninth-wicket stand with Nathan Lyon set an Australian record against South Africa. Australia then dismissed Ryan Rickelton for a duck before b
sports.content: Matt Renshaw scored a career-best 190 to lift Australia to 390 all out in the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead after the visitors slumped to 124 for six. His 134-run ninth-wicket stand with Nathan Lyon set an Australian record against South Africa. Australia then dismissed Ryan Rickelton for a duck before bad light ended play with the hosts 27 for one, 363 runs behind. South Africa reached 85 for two on day three, with David Bedingham on 47, after Mitchell Starc had Aiden Markram caught by Renshaw for 37. The hosts were still 305 runs short of Australia’s total, with Temba Bavuma newly at the crease alongside Bedingham.
sports.image_alt: Matt Renshaw’s 190 lifts Australia after collapse in Durban Test

sports.title: Ten-man Brighton beat Sunderland 2-0 to extend winning run
sports.summary: Brighton beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light on Oct. 10 despite losing Pascal Struijk to a red card in the 57th minute. Maxim De Cuyper put Brighton ahead in the 53rd minute, and substitute Jaouen Hadjam sealed the win in stoppage time. Brighton’s third consecutive Premier League win moved them to third place w
sports.content: Brighton beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light on Oct. 10 despite losing Pascal Struijk to a red card in the 57th minute. Maxim De Cuyper put Brighton ahead in the 53rd minute, and substitute Jaouen Hadjam sealed the win in stoppage time. Brighton’s third consecutive Premier League win moved them to third place with 13 points, two points behind joint leaders Manchester City and Arsenal. Sunderland remained in 16th with four points after failing to capitalise on their extra-man advantage. Brighton next travel to Portugal for a Europa League match against Torreense on Thursday.
sports.image_alt: Ten-man Brighton beat Sunderland 2-0 to extend winning run

sports.title: Ajer’s late equaliser preserves Brentford’s unbeaten start against Aston Villa
sports.summary: Kristoffer Ajer scored in the 79th minute to earn Brentford a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa on Saturday, keeping Keith Andrews’ side unbeaten after six Premier League matches. Villa went ahead in the 77th minute after cancelling out Brentford’s opener but could not secure their first home league win of the season. The draw g
sports.content: Kristoffer Ajer scored in the 79th minute to earn Brentford a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa on Saturday, keeping Keith Andrews’ side unbeaten after six Premier League matches. Villa went ahead in the 77th minute after cancelling out Brentford’s opener but could not secure their first home league win of the season. The draw gave them their first home point of the campaign. Yehor Yarmolyuk opened the scoring for Brentford before Nicolas Jackson equalised. John McGinn put Villa ahead, but Ajer responded two minutes later, finishing after combining with Jaidon Anthony. Villa defender Matteo Ruggeri left the match with a hamstring injury and was due to be assessed after tests on Sunday.
sports.image_alt: Ajer’s late equaliser preserves Brentford’s unbeaten start against Aston Villa

sports.title: Guardians erase 2-0 deficit, eliminate White Sox and reach ALCS
sports.summary: The Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 in Saturday’s decisive Game 5 at Progressive Field, winning their American League Division Series 3-2 after losing the first two games. sports.content: The Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 in Saturday’s decisive Game 5 at Progressive Field, winning their American League Division Series 3-2 after losing the first two games. José Ramírez hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning, and starter Gavin Williams struck out 12 while allowing one hit over 5⅔ innings. Cleveland’s relievers preserved the shutout. Cleveland became the 11th team to win a best-of-five postseason series after falling behind 0-2, and the first since the 2017 Yankees. The Guardians shut out Chicago in the winner-take-all game, ending the White Sox’s season. Chicago had reached the playoffs after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. The Guardians visit the Tampa Bay Rays for ALCS Game 1 on Monday, Oct. 12. Tampa Bay swept the Yankees in its Division Series, while Cleveland needed all five games to advance.

sports.title: Henderson scores twice as Chelsea beat Bournemouth 5-1 at home
sports.summary: Jordan Henderson scored twice and assisted Morgan Rogers on his home debut for Chelsea as they beat Bournemouth 5-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. sports.content: Jordan Henderson scored twice and assisted Morgan Rogers on his home debut for Chelsea as they beat Bournemouth 5-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Henderson opened the scoring after 68 seconds and curled in a free kick for Chelsea’s fifth goal. João Pedro also scored twice, while Evanilson scored Bournemouth’s only goal. The result ended Chelsea’s three-match winless run and moved them to fifth on 10 points. Bournemouth remained 17th with three points and no wins in their opening six league matches. The match also gave Xabi Alonso his first look at Henderson and Moisés Caicedo starting together in midfield. Caicedo returned after a calf problem, but Chelsea conceded from a corner and did not keep a clean sheet. Before the match, Chelsea had conceded 12 goals in their first five league games, the most in the division. Chelsea travel to Everton next week, while Bournemouth host Sunderland. Bournemouth manager Marco Rose said his team had not been sharp enough at the start of either half and accepted responsibility for failing to respond to Chelsea’s fast starts.

sports.content: Max Verstappen won Saturday’s rain-hit Singapore sprint, then secured pole for Sunday’s Grand Prix with a 1:31.373 lap, beating Charles Leclerc by 0.054 seconds. It was Verstappen’s 50th career pole and his first victory in Singapore. Lewis Hamilton qualified third, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli fourth. George Russell briefly led the sprint but crashed on the opening lap, scoring no points and bringing out the safety car. Verstappen took control at the restart and finished ahead of Hamilton and Leclerc. A last-lap collision between McLaren teammates Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri ended Piastri’s race and dropped Norris to eighth; stewards took no action. Antonelli finished fourth in the sprint and qualified fourth, leaving him 89 points ahead of Russell, who will start Sunday’s Grand Prix from the back after an engine penalty. If Antonelli leaves Singapore 101 points clear, he can clinch the title at the next round in Austin.

sports.content: French rider Paul Seixas won Il Lombardia on Saturday, October 10, attacking on the Civiglio climb with about 19 kilometres remaining and finishing 48 seconds ahead of Vuelta champion Enric Mas. Giulio Ciccone finished third. At 20, Seixas became the youngest winner in the race’s history and the youngest Monument winner since 1944. Before the race, riders in Bergamo delayed the start by five minutes to demand action on vehicle-related dangers. They cited the August death of British rider Finlay Tarling after a collision with a vehicle at the Tour of Portugal, and an incident earlier that week in which a police motorcycle struck Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi during the Tre Valli Varesine. Seixas’s win capped a season in which he also finished fourth in his Tour de France debut and won the Tour of the Basque Country and La Flèche Wallonne. The riders’ union urged cycling’s governing body, the UCI, to press race organisers to take concrete safety measures. A UCI reform process discussed in a recent consultation may not lead to changes before 2029.

sports.content: Carlos Alcaraz beat Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-3 in 66 minutes on Saturday to reach the Shanghai Masters third round, four days after winning the Tokyo Open. The second seed, who returned this season from a right-wrist injury, has won seven straight matches and will next face Belgium’s Zizou Bergs. Daniil Medvedev also advanced, coming from a set down to defeat Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 in his first match since his disqualification in Beijing. He was disqualified from his China Open semifinal against Novak Djokovic after a ball he hit into the stands struck a spectator. He said the incident was accidental and apologized. Felix Auger-Aliassime won a nearly three-hour match against Camilo Ugo Carabelli, while defending champion Valentin Vacherot opened with a straight-sets win over Sebastián Báez. World number one Jannik Sinner withdrew from Shanghai and said he would miss the rest of 2026 because of a right-knee injury. Rain interrupted play on outside courts, and Alcaraz’s next match is scheduled for Monday.
